title: Neural networks and deep learning, in brief

sentences.text: Purpose.
sentences.say: Purpose.

sentences.text: Large language models are neural networks, so before the agent chapters you should know the parts.
sentences.say: Large language models are neural networks, so before the agent chapters you should know the parts.

sentences.text: Good news: you already know the first one.
sentences.say: Good news: you already know the first one.

sentences.text: A single neuron is a logistic regression.
sentences.say: A single neuron is a logistic regression.

sentences.text: Key ideas
sentences.say: Key ideas

sentences.text: A neuron computes a weighted sum plus a bias, then passes it through an activation function.
sentences.say: A neuron computes a weighted sum plus a bias, then passes it through an activation function.

sentences.text: Layers of neurons learn their own features.
sentences.say: Layers of neurons learn their own features.

sentences.text: Many layers is what "deep" means.
sentences.say: Many layers is what "deep" means.

sentences.text: Without a non-linear activation, any number of layers collapses into one linear model.
sentences.say: Without a non-linear activation, any number of layers collapses into one linear model.

sentences.text: Training is gradient descent, with the slopes for all layers computed by backpropagation.
sentences.say: Training is gradient descent, with the slopes for all layers computed by backpropagation.

sentences.text: For tables of data, trees often win.
sentences.say: For tables of data, trees often win.

sentences.text: Neural networks shine on images, text, audio and other unstructured data.
sentences.say: Neural networks shine on images, text, audio and other unstructured data.

sentences.text: 14.1 One neuron
sentences.say: 14.1 One neuron

sentences.text: A neuron takes the features, multiplies each by a weight, adds a bias, and applies an activation function g:
sentences.say: A neuron takes the features, multiplies each by a weight, adds a bias, and applies an activation function g:

sentences.text: With g as the sigmoid this is exactly logistic regression (Chapter 9).
sentences.say: With g as the sigmoid this is exactly logistic regression (Chapter 9).

sentences.text: Example: inputs x = [2, -1], weights w = [0.5, 0.25], bias b = 0.1.
sentences.say: Example: inputs x equals 2, -1, weights w equals 0.5, 0.25, bias b equals 0.1.
Then z equals 2 times 0.5 plus (-1) times 0.25 plus 0.1 equals 0.85.

sentences.text: With the ReLU activation (max of 0 and z) the output is 0.85; with the sigmoid it is 0.701.
sentences.say: With the ReLU activation (max of 0 and z) the output is 0.85; with the sigmoid it is 0.701.

sentences.text: 14.2 Layers learn features
sentences.say: 14.2 Layers learn features

sentences.text: Stack neurons into a layer, and layers into a network.
sentences.say: Stack neurons into a layer, and layers into a network.

sentences.text: The first layer looks at the raw inputs.
sentences.say: The first layer looks at the raw inputs.

sentences.text: The next layer looks at the outputs of the first, and so on.
sentences.say: The next layer looks at the outputs of the first, and so on.

sentences.text: In an image network (Shaw Talebi's example) the first layers detect edges, the next combine edges into eyes and whiskers, and the last decides "cat".
sentences.say: In an image network (Shaw Talebi's example) the first layers detect edges, the next combine edges into eyes and whiskers, and the last decides "cat".

sentences.text: Nobody tells the network to look for whiskers: it finds the features that help.
sentences.say: Nobody tells the network to look for whiskers: it finds the features that help.

sentences.text: This is why deep learning needs far less hand-made feature engineering than the traditional models of Chapter 13 (Chapter 8's feature work is exactly what it automates).
sentences.say: This is why deep learning needs far less hand-made feature engineering than the traditional models of Chapter 13 (Chapter 8's feature work is exactly what it automates).

sentences.text: The activation must be non-linear.
sentences.say: The activation must be non-linear.

sentences.text: Two linear layers in a row, W2 (W1 x), equal one linear layer with weights (W2 W1), so without a non-linear function in between, depth adds nothing.
sentences.say: Two linear layers in a row, W2 (W1 x), equal one linear layer with weights (W2 W1), so without a non-linear function in between, depth adds nothing.

sentences.text: The non-linearity is what lets a network learn almost any pattern.
sentences.say: The non-linearity is what lets a network learn almost any pattern.

sentences.text: 14.3 Training
sentences.say: 14.3 Training

sentences.text: Training is the gradient descent of Chapter 6 on a cost function, with two additions:
sentences.say: Training is the gradient descent of Chapter 6 on a cost function, with two additions:

sentences.text: Backpropagation computes the slope of the cost with respect to every weight in every layer.
sentences.say: Backpropagation computes the slope of the cost with respect to every weight in every layer.

sentences.text: It uses the chain rule of calculus: it runs the network forward to get a prediction and the cost, then backward, passing the slopes from the last layer to the first.
sentences.say: It uses the chain rule of calculus: it runs the network forward to get a prediction and the cost, then backward, passing the slopes from the last layer to the first.

sentences.text: You do not code this by hand: libraries such as PyTorch do it automatically.
sentences.say: You do not code this by hand: libraries such as PyTorch do it automatically.

sentences.text: Mini-batches and Adam.
sentences.say: Mini-batches and Adam.

sentences.text: Each step uses a small batch of examples (8 to 32 in Shaw's example), and the optimizer Adam adapts the step size per parameter (Chapter 6).
sentences.say: Each step uses a small batch of examples (8 to 32 in Shaw's example), and the optimizer Adam adapts the step size per parameter (Chapter 6).

sentences.text: The usual hyperparameters are the number of epochs (passes over the data), the learning rate, the batch size and dropout, a regularizer that randomly switches off some neurons during training so that the network cannot rely on any one of them (Chapter 11).
sentences.say: The usual hyperparameters are the number of epochs (passes over the data), the learning rate, the batch size and dropout, a regularizer that randomly switches off some neurons during training so that the network cannot rely on any one of them (Chapter 11).

sentences.text: 14.4 Architectures
sentences.say: 14.4 Architectures

sentences.text: A large language model is a very large transformer trained on text to predict the next word.
sentences.say: A large language model is a very large transformer trained on text to predict the next word.

sentences.text: It is trained first on huge amounts of text, then refined with supervised examples and reinforcement learning (Chapter 1).
sentences.say: It is trained first on huge amounts of text, then refined with supervised examples and reinforcement learning (Chapter 1).

sentences.text: 14.5 When to use it
sentences.say: 14.5 When to use it

sentences.text: Use neural networks when the input is unstructured (images, audio, text) and you have a lot of data, or when you can start from a pretrained model, as you will with LLMs and embedding models.
sentences.say: Use neural networks when the input is unstructured (images, audio, text) and you have a lot of data, or when you can start from a pretrained model, as you will with LLMs and embedding models.

sentences.text: For a table of numbers and categories, such as loan data, carefully tuned tree ensembles often match or beat neural networks (Grinsztajn et al. studied this on 45 datasets in Why do tree-based models still outperform deep learning on tabular data?).
sentences.say: For a table of numbers and categories, such as loan data, carefully tuned tree ensembles often match or beat neural networks (Grinsztajn et al. studied this on 45 datasets in Why do tree-based models still outperform deep learning on tabular data?).

sentences.text: Try the forest first.
sentences.say: Try the forest first.

sentences.text: Loan example.
sentences.say: Loan example.

sentences.text: To read scanned payslips and extract the income, use a neural network (a pretrained vision or language model).
sentences.say: To read scanned payslips and extract the income, use a neural network (a pretrained vision or language model).

sentences.text: To predict whether a customer accepts an offer from a table of 15 columns, start with logistic regression and a gradient-boosted forest.
sentences.say: To predict whether a customer accepts an offer from a table of 15 columns, start with logistic regression and a gradient-boosted forest.

sentences.say: Common mistakes

sentences.text: Thinking "deep" means "better".
sentences.say: Thinking "deep" means "better".

sentences.text: Training a big network from scratch on a few thousand rows.
sentences.say: Training a big network from scratch on a few thousand rows.

sentences.text: Forgetting that a network needs the same care as any model: a baseline, scaled inputs, a validation set.
